final_candidates.decision_summary: Replacing W17 with an acidic residue removes a bulky aromatic side chain and could strongly destabilize hydrophobic packing. Burial is unverified, so folding disruption and knockout are not established.
Introducing proline at I33 in the hydrophobic GIIYPVIV segment could disrupt backbone geometry and hydrogen bonding. Nearby native P35 makes the local structural effect uncertain.

Replacing F48 with an acidic residue could remove an aromatic packing interaction and destabilize folding. Its glycine/serine-rich surroundings leave open the possibility of solvent exposure and substitution tolerance.

stop_reason.detail: The strongest sequence-based candidates have been retained, and additional self-iteration cannot resolve their unknown structural environments.

history.rationale: Replacing the bulky aromatic W17 with an acidic residue could disrupt hydrophobic packing and introduce an unfavorable charge. Its impact depends on burial, which cannot be established from sequence alone.
W17 is verified in the supplied sequence. Replacing a bulky aromatic residue with an acidic residue could disrupt hydrophobic packing, although burial is unverified.

Introducing proline into the hydrophobic segment around I33 could disrupt backbone hydrogen bonding and local secondary structure. This is a strong folding-disruption hypothesis, although the local structure is unverified.
I33 is verified in the hydrophobic GIIYPVIV segment. Proline could disrupt backbone hydrogen bonding and local geometry, but nearby native P35 makes the secondary-structure context uncertain.
F48D removes an aromatic side chain and introduces a negative charge, potentially weakening core packing. The prediction is less certain if F48 is solvent exposed.
F48 is verified in the supplied sequence. Aromatic-to-acidic replacement could remove a packing anchor, although its glycine/serine-rich surroundings leave solvent exposure uncertain.
Y34D introduces an acidic side chain into a hydrophobic-rich segment and removes aromatic packing capacity. A buried position would make this substitution particularly destabilizing.
Y34 is verified and lies within a hydrophobic segment. Introducing an acidic side chain could destabilize packing, but neither burial nor a folding effect is established.

V38P could destabilize an extended structural segment through backbone restriction and loss of an amide hydrogen-bond donor. Its effect depends on whether V38 participates in regular secondary structure.
V38 is verified in the supplied sequence. Proline introduces a plausible backbone-disruption mechanism, conditional on this position participating in regular secondary structure.
Replacing F60 with aspartate could disrupt hydrophobic contacts that anchor the C-terminal region. Sequence alone does not establish whether those contacts exist.
F60 is verified in the supplied sequence. Removing an aromatic side chain could destabilize the fold, but the nearby polar and acidic residues make a surface-tolerated substitution plausible.

Y16P combines removal of an aromatic side chain with a backbone-constraining substitution near the YWY motif. It could impair folding if this region contributes to regular secondary structure or core packing.
Y16 is verified in the supplied sequence. This substitution removes an aromatic side chain and constrains the backbone, but proline tolerance cannot be inferred reliably without structural context.

G54W introduces substantial steric bulk into a glycine-rich region and could prevent a tight backbone turn. This is more speculative because the region might instead accommodate the substitution through flexibility.
G54 is verified as the second glycine in AGGL. Tryptophan could obstruct a tight turn, but a flexible exposed loop could accommodate it.
